bull.b: The 20-year PPA secures a critical input for Phase 1 and supports planned power availability in Q3 2027. Long-duration contracted supply can improve project bankability, reduce power procurement uncertainty, and strengthen NUAI’s ability to attract a technology tenant.

Full Phase 1 permitting and active clearing and grading move the project beyond an early concept and reduce a major execution hurdle. Continued site progress provides tangible evidence that NUAI is converting its development plan into infrastructure capable of supporting future revenue.

A planned 757 MW platform gives NUAI substantial room to scale beyond the initial project and pursue multiple phases of data-center development. The expansion opportunity is supported by secured Phase 1 power and a site strategy designed to improve capacity and utility build-out flexibility.

bear.b: The sharp revenue contraction and deeply negative margins indicate that NUAI’s current operating model is not yet generating a stable earnings base. Until project development converts into recurring leases or operating revenue, weak scale and widening losses remain substantial fundamental risks.

Negative operating and free cash flow mean NUAI is consuming cash rather than funding operations internally. Continued burn can increase dependence on external capital, restrict flexibility during project execution, and make funding terms more important to the timing and economics of future growth.

The project’s commercial and expansion plans still depend on unresolved milestones, including execution of the definitive Phase 1 lease and approval of the Phase 2 air permit. Delays could defer construction, financing, tenant commitments, and the transition from development spending to revenue.
